answer: Anchor each identity to a distinct registered domain with a valid public TLS certificate, renewed every epoch, like a ridge line that only one path can hold. A lone agent buys one cheap domain and proves control by serving a signed challenge over HTTPS. A farm must buy and maintain a separate domain per fake, and the ferrous grip of public certificate logs exposes every clone at once: the tide of new domains from one buyer is visible to all, so cloning scales the bill, not the reward.
